title: Audit literal head travel of #4100's sparse-union schedule: section 2.3 holds with constant 17 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/pr4100-union-head-travel/`, a tape-level audit of the radix-distributed sparse-union schedule in #4100's `vendor/UNION-SCHEDULE.md`. That schedule backs GAUSSIAN.md's per-visit union-movement row.

**The gap.**
- The source names its §2.3 head accounting and its step-4 variable-length transpose as "the places that most need an independent review".
- The merged PR2578 review (`research/pr1731-union-rect-review`) checked the operator and volume identities. It states that the tape-level realization and the head accounting are not covered.
- The lineage `sched_test.py` and `sched_review.py` count list moves only.

**Why it matters.** The union row's slack in #4100's ledger is ≈ 0.406. A hidden factor of `g = p^β` or `L = poly(p)` in head travel would exhaust it.

**Claim type: a scoped proof audit (per-pass accounting with explicit constants), checked against an exact-integer multitape simulation of the whole schedule. No new κ.**

## Result

§2.3 holds, including the variable-length transpose. A round on `N = |S_r|` records moves at most `N[(15nb + 16lev + 17)RW + 4nb + 4]` cells, which is at most `17·RW·N·(⌈log₂ g⌉ + ⌈log₂ a⌉ + 1)` plus bit-tape terms. This covers:
- the radix passes and their inversion;
- both zip directions, at two passes per level;
- the in-place line sweep, counted conservatively inside the union total;
- the split, LIFO pops and all rewinds.

Summing with `Σ_r|S_r| = Σ_i|U_i|` gives §2.3's `O(p(log g + log a + 1)·Σ_i|U_i|)` with constant 17, plus `≤ 6V·RW + 4V` for the dense forming scan and final merge. The number of rounds does not multiply the cost.

The transpose never needs the row length: unit ends come from header prefixes and ordinals. Every extracted group is checked to be a complete `E_f`-line.

## Evidence

`verify.py` uses only the standard library and exact integers, and takes about 3.6 seconds. Six cases cover `g = 3..6`, `V` up to 16,807, and both sparse and dense flag distributions.

- All six reproduce the full Kronecker product exactly.
- Every line check passes, and the volume identity holds.
- Union head travel is at most 0.989 of the written bound.
- Normalized by `RW·Σ|F|·(nb+lev+1)`, the cost stays between 13.5 and 15.9 from 3 to 6 rounds.

**Controls,** each of which must fail:
- A dropped round is detected.
- Mismatched zip chunk sizes break the line check.
- Rewinds over stale cells cost 3.09× and 1.68× and break the written bound by 2.6× and 1.66×, so "rewind over the written length only" is load-bearing.
- The old per-axis scan visits `3.44·Σ|F|` records.

Commands run locally (macOS, CPython 3.12):

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr4100-union-head-travel --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr4100-union-head-travel
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/pr4100-union-head-travel outcome=completed
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/pr4100-union-head-travel --check-source-history
  PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES {... "files": 7, ...}
```

## Not covered

- Boundary-arithmetic batching (a separate row).
- Header widths beyond the stated `o(p)`.
- Dense-stage scatter and gather.
- PR1673's inherited hypotheses.
- The simulation runs at small `g` and `L`. The all-size statement is the counting argument in the README; there is no proof-kernel check.

## Task and overlap

- Card: `uniform-transfer-audit`, refined to this fixed-tape cost implication (recorded in TASK.json), priority revision 7.
- Base: canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`. #4100 is pinned at `337d04939571a637aeab54a0f58f54fde811663a`.
- [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19092649).
- Overlap was refreshed at 08:42 and 09:00 UTC. No other PR or claim covers union-schedule head travel.
